english.html: eft, through want and necessity; a blasphemy against God, slander against the Prince, insult against one's neighbour, through a slip and looseness of the tongue: but a calumny is always deliberate, conspired and maliciously premeditated; in detestation of which the Lord God was not content to instruct us by the mouth of Moses to build no calumny against our neighbour <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>, but has moreover straitly commanded us to deliver the oppressed from the hand of the calumniator, lest his indignation go forth like fire, and, kindled by the malice of such affections, there be found afterwards none who can quench it <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>. Likewise he has given several great and proper epithets to Satan, to show his cruelty and malicious cunning; as when he has called him Serpent <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>, Dragon <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>, Asp <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>, ravening and roaring Lion <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>; but among them all he has not wished to forget the one that is most fitting to him, namely, to name him Calumniator, <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup> inasmuch as he is a liar and false accuser, who strives incessantly only to throw our conscience into confusion, to make us find evil what by the grace of God we have done well; and on the contrary, exalting and magnifying our evil works, only to keep and harden us in them. There is certainly no crime in a commonwealth worthy of being punished and repressed with so great severity as a calumny: and yet in this wretched age of ours it is made a game of, and the reins are found so slackened for calumniators that it is as it were permitted them, with impunity, to conspire, contrive and machinate all kinds of ruses, wiles and wickednesses against good people. O noble saying of Domitian, who said that the prince who does not chastise calumniators lends a hand to their malice and upholds them <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>. Alexander the Great, when he presided at the judgment of capital crimes, was accustomed, to obviate calumnies, to stop one of his ears with his hand, in order to keep it whole and free from all calumny for the accused; and if he could hear, or only smell the odour of some calumny, he was inflamed with anger so bitterly that he often became cruel and inexorable.

notes.gloss: Deliver the oppressed from the hand of the calumniator (Vulgate calumniantis), lest my indignation go forth like fire and burn, and there be none to quench it, because of the malice of your doings.
The serpent of Eden; "that old serpent, called the Devil and Satan".

notes.citation: Psalm 90 (Vulgate numbering; = Psalm 91:13, super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis)

Ezekiel 22 (22:25); Zephaniah 3 (3:3); 1 Peter 5 (5:8); Psalm 21 (Vulgate; = 22:13, sicut leo rapiens et rugiens); the closing "& c. iij" not resolved (perhaps Vulgate Psalm 7:3, ne quando rapiat ut leo)
notes.original: Ezeciel xxij. Saphonie iij. A la premiere S. Pierre c. v. Pſaume xxj. & c. iij.
notes.gloss: The ravening and roaring lion; 1 Peter: the devil as a roaring lion seeking whom he may devour.

notes.citation: Psalm 11 (Vulgate numbering), as printed; the bearing is not evident (the usual texts for Satan the accuser are Vulgate Psalm 108:6, diabolus stet a dextris eius, and Revelation 12:10, accusator fratrum nostrorum); number unverified

notes.original: Suetone en la vie de Domitian.
notes.gloss: Princeps qui delatores non castigat, irritat — a prince who does not punish informers eggs them on.

notes.citation: Digest 48.4.7.3 (Ad legem Iuliam maiestatis, l. Famosi, Modestinus)
notes.original: l. famoſi. D. ad l. Iul. maie ſta.
notes.gloss: Nec lubricum linguae ad poenam facile trahendum est — a slip of the tongue is not readily to be drawn to punishment; it belongs to "slander against the Prince … through a slip and looseness of the tongue".
